hints: Focus on two things at once, the number of carbon atoms and the functional group that can become a carboxylic acid in one step.
Propanoic acid has 3 carbons, so first eliminate any starting material that does not have 3 carbons in the right skeleton.
Remember which functional group oxidises directly to a carboxylic acid in one step, and check which option fits that pattern.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target**

Think about what propanoic acid looks like. It is a 3-carbon carboxylic acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.

So we need a 3-carbon starting material that can change into $\text{-COOH}$ in just one reaction.

**Recall the one-step routes to acids**

The classic one-step route is oxidation of an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{R-CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{R-COOH}$$
This uses acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ with heating, or Tollens reagent.

**Apply to propanal**

Propanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, a 3-carbon aldehyde. Gentle oxidation gives the 3-carbon acid directly.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
That is propanoic acid in a single reaction, so this is our match.

options.A: Ethanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$. Acid hydrolysis does give a carboxylic acid in one step, but it gives ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) with only 2 carbons. It cannot grow the chain to make 3-carbon propanoic acid.
options.B: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Oxidation gives the ketone propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, not a carboxylic acid. Secondary alcohols cannot be oxidised to acids without breaking C-C bonds.
options.C: Propanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. It has the correct 3-carbon skeleton and aldehydes oxidise in one step to carboxylic acids with the same number of carbons. Oxidation gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, propanoic acid.
options.D: Propyl ethanoate is the ester $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Hydrolysis in one step gives ethanoic acid plus propan-1-ol, not propanoic acid. The acid part comes from the ethanoate side, which has only 2 carbons.
